name: Hardware Monitor + Storage
author: zoltanf (fork of meviusisback/omarchy-hw-monitor; original by Edgar Silva)
description: GPU, CPU, temperature, and RAM in the bar as sleek icon + figure readouts, with a first-class visual system panel including top processes by RAM (with grouping off, per-tab hints for Chromium-family browsers) and free space on every mounted disk and share.

barWidget.description: GPU, CPU, temperature, and RAM load as sleek icon readouts, vertical gauges, or spelled out words. Left click opens the system telemetry panel with top processes by RAM and free space per mounted disk, removable drive and network share, and — with the Group toggle off — per-tab hints for Chromium-family browsers (it reads their process memory where the kernel allows it, and caches those labels plus the last CPU snapshot in a 0600 file in your runtime dir, which on a default setup is tmpfs and is cleared at logout).

schema.label: Readout
schema.description: icons is sleek icon + figures + temperature; compact is glyph + gauge; full adds the temperature; labels spells the readout out as words. Right-clicking the widget cycles them.

schema.label: Item sequence
schema.description: Order of telemetry items in the bar, comma-separated: 'gpu,cpu,cpu-temp,ram' or 'gpu,cpu,cpu-temp,gpu-temp,ram'.

schema.label: Show GPU load
schema.description: Show GPU load in the top bar (hidden automatically if no GPU card is found).

schema.label: Show CPU load
schema.description: Show CPU load percentage in the top bar.

schema.label: Show CPU temperature
schema.description: Show CPU temperature with thermometer icon.

schema.label: Show GPU temperature
schema.description: Show GPU temperature in the top bar.

schema.label: Show memory
schema.description: Show RAM / memory usage.

schema.label: Show top processes
schema.description: Show the top processes by RAM in the system panel (sampled only while the panel is open).

schema.label: Top process count
schema.description: How many processes to list in the top-processes section (3-12, sorted by the active metric).

schema.label: Top process metric
schema.description: Sort top processes by CPU load or RAM.

schema.label: Group by application
schema.description: Collapse processes by application (systemd scope, comm-name fallback) with summed RAM/CPU and process counts. Turn it off to see the per-tab role and domain hints instead.

schema.label: Show storage
schema.description: Show free space for every mounted disk, removable drive and network share in the system panel (sampled only while the panel is open; idle automounts are not triggered).

schema.label: Storage: hidden mount points
schema.description: Comma-separated mount points left out of the Storage section. The EFI system partition is hidden by default.

schema.label: Panel section order
schema.description: Order of the system panel sections, comma-separated. Missing ones are appended. Easier from the panel's gear settings.

schema.label: Hidden panel sections
schema.description: Comma-separated panel sections to hide (dials, history, processor, memory, storage, procs, gpu).

schema.label: Pause when idle (s)
schema.description: Stop sampling after this many seconds without keyboard or mouse input (screensaver, lock, screen off), unless the panel is open. A playing video counts as activity. 0 never pauses.

schema.label: Folded panel sections
schema.description: Comma-separated panel sections shown folded to their header (history, processor, memory, storage, procs, gpu). Clicking a section's header edits this.

schema.label: Panel dial order
schema.description: Order of the round dials at the top of the panel, comma-separated.

schema.label: Hidden panel dials
schema.description: Comma-separated dials to hide (cpu, ram, gpu).

schema.label: Memory format
schema.description: 'used/total' (12/23G), 'used' (12.3G), 'percent' (52%), 'free' (11.1G), or 'available' (11.1G).

schema.label: Temperature format
schema.description: 'degree-unit' (45°C/113°F), 'degree' (45°), 'unit' (45C), 'unit-lower' (45c), or 'bare' (45).

schema.label: Use Fahrenheit (°F)
schema.description: Display temperatures in Fahrenheit (°F) instead of Celsius (°C).

schema.label: Percentage padding
schema.description: How percentages hold width: 'none' (natural flow), 'zero' (03%), 'lead' ( 3%), or 'trail'. Figure cells always reserve slot width in every mode.

schema.label: Show vertical gauges
schema.description: Show vertical battery-style capsule gauges in the bar.

schema.label: Show figures with gauges
schema.description: Put numeric figures beside vertical gauges in compact and full modes.

schema.label: Show clock speeds
schema.description: CPU average clock across all threads, and GPU core clock, in GHz.

schema.label: Sample interval on battery (seconds)
schema.description: Used while the laptop runs on battery. Never faster than the sample interval above. The open panel samples every 2 s on battery.

schema.label: Percentage pad opacity
schema.description: Opacity of the padded percentage background (0-1).

schema.label: GPU glyph rotation (deg)
schema.description: Rotate the GPU glyph (0, 90, 180, 270).

schema.label: CPU glyph rotation (deg)
schema.description: Rotate the CPU glyph (0, 90, 180, 270).

schema.label: Temperature glyph rotation (deg)
schema.description: Rotate the temperature glyph (0, 90, 180, 270).

schema.label: Memory glyph rotation (deg)
schema.description: Rotate the memory glyph (0, 90, 180, 270).

schema.label: Icon size (px)
schema.description: 0 follows the theme's bar icon size.

schema.label: GPU card preference
schema.description: 'auto' prefers the card driving connected displays; 'busiest' follows the NVIDIA card with the highest load; otherwise use an index ('0', '1') or name substring.

schema.label: Monitors
schema.description: Which screens to draw on by connector name (e.g. 'DP-1,HDMI-A-1'). Empty means all screens.

schema.label: Left click runs
schema.description: Shell command run on left click via 'bash -lc' as you, unsandboxed. Leave empty to open the built-in system telemetry panel. Only set it from a source you trust: anything that can write this widget's settings can run code on your next click.
